sections.heading: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: This Test Plan defines the overall testing strategy, scope, schedule, and responsibilities for (S)TeemBang, a fitness tracking web application developed by Group 4 for the Software Development course (AY 2025–2026).

The system enables health-conscious users to register and authenticate securely, track steps and workouts, set daily/weekly/monthly goals, view analytics dashboards, manage profiles (including avatar upload and daily targets for steps, calories, and workouts), receive notifications, and allows administrators to monitor member activity and platform metrics.

Technology stack under test: Vue 3 + Vite frontend, FastAPI backend, SQLAlchemy + SQLite database, JWT authentication. Testing follows IEEE 829-1998 principles adapted for an Agile (Scrum) delivery model.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
paragraphs: In scope: user registration/login (member and admin roles), profile management with photo upload, activity logging (steps sync, workout timer, calorie logging), goal creation and metric-specific tracking, dashboard daily goal rings, analytics trends, notifications, admin console with per-user daily progress, API integration tests (PyTest), security (JWT, role-based access), usability on desktop browsers, and basic performance of API responses under development load.

Out of scope: wearable device APIs (Apple Health, Google Fit), payment/subscription processing, AI coaching, nutrition engine, native mobile app store deployment, load testing beyond 50 concurrent simulated users, and third-party OAuth providers.

sections.heading: 6. Approach and Strategy
bullets: Unit/Component: PyTest automated tests on FastAPI routes and service functions
Integration: API tests exercising auth → activities → goals → analytics flow
System: End-to-end manual and automated validation against functional requirements FR1–FR8
UAT: Business scenarios executed by non-developer classmates acting as fitness users
Regression: Re-execution of failed/affected test cases after defect fixes
Tools: PyTest, FastAPI TestClient, Vue/Vite dev server, Chrome/Edge browsers, python-docx/openpyxl for documentation

sections.heading: 7. Pass / Fail Criteria
bullets: Pass: Actual result matches expected result; no severity Critical/High open defects for the feature
Fail: Incorrect data, unauthorized access, crash, or missing required UI/API behavior
Automated API tests must achieve 100% pass rate before system test sign-off
UAT requires ≥85% pass rate on business scenarios with no Critical open defects

sections.heading: 13. Test Levels and Types
paragraphs: Testing is organized into four levels aligned with the V-model and Agile sprint cadence. Each level has defined entry/exit criteria and assigned owners.

Unit testing focuses on isolated backend functions (calorie estimation, goal progress calculation, JWT token creation). Integration testing validates API route chains using FastAPI TestClient with an in-memory or file SQLite database. System testing exercises the full stack through the browser against seeded demo data. User acceptance testing validates business scenarios from a non-developer perspective.

sections.heading: 15. Suspension and Resumption Criteria
bullets: Testing will be suspended if more than 30% of planned test cases fail in a single cycle, indicating a build instability.
Testing will be suspended if a Critical defect blocks login or data persistence for all users.
Testing resumes after a new build is deployed, release notes are published, and affected test cases are identified for regression.
A suspension log entry must be recorded in the Defect Log with date, reason, and responsible developer.

sections.heading: 16. Defect Management Process
paragraphs: All defects discovered during any test phase are logged in Doc 7 (Defect / Bug Report Log) with a unique ID (DEF-xxx), severity, steps to reproduce, and status. Severity definitions: Critical — system unusable or data loss; High — major feature broken with no workaround; Medium — feature impaired with workaround; Low — cosmetic or minor UX issue.

Developers assign fixes to a build number. QA verifies closure and updates the Verified By and Date Closed fields. Open Critical or High defects block UAT exit unless explicitly deferred with instructor approval.
